result.rationale: In packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the diff replaces hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken (which resolves to a HubspotToken object) with refreshOAuthTokens. That helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns the raw fetch `response` from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT when sharing is enabled — a Fetch Response, not a parsed HubspotToken. The caller then reads hubspotRefreshToken fields, which would be undefined on a Response object, breaking the refresh flow in the credential-sharing path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call in refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns the response directly from either the sync endpoint fetch or the refreshFunction. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it returns a fetch Response object. When false, it returns whatever refreshFunction returns - which in HubSpot's case is the result of hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(), which is a HubspotToken object. The code then assigns this to hubspotRefreshToken typed as HubspotToken and accesses properties like .expiresIn. When the sync branch is taken, the Response object won't have these HubspotToken properties, causing undefined values and broken credential persistence.
